newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent edges up but thin, resistance at $22.75.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent edges up but thin, resistance at $22.75.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ticked slightly higher in quiet mid-afternoon trade but volumes traded were low and sharp price changes are unlikely, dealers said.
"It's pretty much 'steady as she goes,'" said Alastair Harris of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.

January Brent was up three cents at $22.63 a barrel at 1529 GMT, in a range from $22.49 at midday to $22.66 by mid-afternoon. "The market continues to find support at these lower levels and we don't see much sign of weakness on the products," said Harris who pegged first resistance on Brent at $22.75 and then the range $22.85 to $22.90.
The market was quiet due partly due to the lack of arbitrage business. NYMEX is shut due to the Thanksgiving holiday and the IPE is closing early at 1730 GMT.
The spot market for prompt Brent cargoes was little changed, talking some 35 cents above January and dealers said no deals had been heard by mid-afternoon.
The oil market barely flinched on Thursday after OPEC agreed to freeze output and Iraq prepared to resume selling oil for the first time in six years.
Some dealers believe the weather in Europe and the U.S. will be pivotal to the next price move.

Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said on Friday a cold November had resulted in higher than normal heating demand in the northeast U.S. but milder temperatures were seen for early December.
December gas oil was up $1.25 at $218.75 a tonne at 1532 GMT, at the day's high.
The physical Rotterdam barge market was very quiet with no change to premiums of $2.00 a tonne above the IPE for prompt.
